ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p347/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p347/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p347/r5.claim: Readings differ on tukhliquna and afkan; Ibn ʿAbbās says making idols is called falsehood because their makers falsely claim they are gods.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p347/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: وتخلقون إفكا، هو نحت الأصنام وخلقها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p347/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p347/r6.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p347/r6.claim: Mujāhid takes “fabricating falsehood” as inventing lies about idols and other matters; al-Zamakhsharī gives alternative grammatical analyses of afkan.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p347/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هو اختلاف الكذب في أمر الأوثان وغير ذلك.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p348/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p348/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p348/r1.claim: The verse argues that idols cannot provide sustenance, whether rizq means the act of provision or the provision itself; God owns all sustenance, so people should seek it from Him and give thanks.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p348/r1.anchor: فقرر أن الأصنام لا ترزق، والرزق يحتمل أن يريد به المصدر

RAZI-FULL:v25p40/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p40/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p40/r1.claim: Razi says Abraham refutes idolatry by considering why anything is worshipped: because it deserves worship in itself, benefits worshippers now or later, or inspires fear.
RAZI-FULL:v25p40/r1.anchor: وذلك لأن المعبود إنما يعبد لأحد أمور

RAZI-FULL:v25p40/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p40/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p40/r2.claim: Idols do not merit worship in themselves because they are merely idols and have no honor or dignity.
RAZI-FULL:v25p40/r2.anchor: لا تستحق العبادة لذاتها لكونها أوثانا لا شرف لها

RAZI-FULL:v25p40/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p40/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p40/r3.claim: Idols cannot benefit people by bringing them into existence, since their worshippers themselves fashion and carve them.
RAZI-FULL:v25p40/r3.anchor: لأن وجودهم منكم حيث تخلقونها وتنحتونها

RAZI-FULL:v25p40/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p40/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p40/r4.claim: Idols cannot sustain life by providing provision; that benefit comes from God, so they offer no present or future benefit.
RAZI-FULL:v25p40/r4.anchor: ولا نفع في البقاء لأن ذلك بالرزق

RAZI-FULL:v25p40/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p40/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
RAZI-FULL:v25p40/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains that indefinite رزقا under negation means idols possess no provision at all, while definite الرزق under affirmation means all provision belongs to God.
RAZI-FULL:v25p40/r5.anchor: قال الزمخشري قال : { لا يملكون لكم رزقا } نكرة في معرض النفي

RAZI-FULL:v25p40/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p40/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p40/r6.claim: Razi offers another distinction: God's provision is known from the promise in 11:6, whereas provision from idols is unknown, explaining the indefinite and definite forms.

RAZI-FULL:v25p40/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p40/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p40/r7.claim: Seeking provision from God recognizes that He alone is worthy in Himself and supplies benefit now and in the future; worship Him for His worth, thank Him for creation and continuing sustenance, and worship Him as the final return and source of hoped-for good.

BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r4.claim: Their objects of worship are manufactured images, with no quality beyond being fashioned statues.
BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r4.anchor: {إنما تعبدون من دون الله أوثانا} هي في نفسها تماثيل مصنوعة لكم ليس فيها وصف غير ذلك

BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r5.claim: Some distinguish an idol (ṣanam), made from wood, gold, or silver in human form, from an image (wathan), made of stone and not in human form.
BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r5.anchor: قال بعضهم : الصنم هو الذي يؤلف من شجر أو ذهب أو فضة في صورة إنسان والوثن

BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r6.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r6.claim: Al-Raghib says khalq is used of people for estimating or for lying; the source also applies it to fabrication with the tongue or by carving idols with the hand.
BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r6.anchor: قال الراغب : الخلق لا يستعمل في كافة الناس إلا على وجهين أحدهما في معنى التقدير والثاني في الكذب

BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r7.claim: Ifk is the worst kind of lie and is named for being turned away from its proper truth.
BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r7.anchor: والإفك أسوأ الكذب وسمي الإفك كذبا لأنه مأفوك أي مصروف عن وجهه

BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r8.claim: They commit a falsehood by calling idols gods and claiming they intercede for them with God; this proves their practice is fabricated and worthless.
BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r8.anchor: والمعنى وتكذبون كذبا حيث تسمونها آلهة وتدعون أنها شفعاؤكم عند الله

BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r9.claim: Malaka means to have power over something; the phrase from Moses means he had power over only himself and his brother (5:25). The indefinite rizq minimizes what idols can provide: nothing.
BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r9.anchor: يقال : ملكت الشيء إذا قدرت عليه ومنه قول موسى : لا أملك إلا نفسي وأخي

BURSEVI:v6p331#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p331#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p331#3/r1.claim: They should seek all provision from God, who alone can deliver it.
BURSEVI:v6p331#3/r1.anchor: {فابتغوا} فاطلبوا {عند الله الرزق} كله فإنه القادر على إيصال الرزق

BURSEVI:v6p331#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p331#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p331#3/r2.claim: Worship God alone and thank Him for His favors; worship carries requests to fulfillment, while gratitude secures blessings and draws further bounty.
BURSEVI:v6p331#3/r2.anchor: {واعبدوه} وحده {واشكروا له} على نعمائه متوسلين إلى مطالبكم بعبادته مقيدين للنعمة بالشكر ومستجلبين للمزيد

BURSEVI:v6p331#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p331#3/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
BURSEVI:v6p331#3/r3.claim: Ibn Ata says provision should be sought through obedience and turning toward worship.
BURSEVI:v6p331#3/r3.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : اطلبوا الرزق بالطاعة والإقبال على العبادة

BURSEVI:v6p331#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p331#3/r4.speaker: سهل
BURSEVI:v6p331#3/r4.claim: Sahl says to seek provision through reliance on God rather than earning, describing this as the way of ordinary people.
BURSEVI:v6p331#3/r4.anchor: وقال سهل : اطلبوا الرزق في التوكل لا في الكسب وهذا سبيل العوام

BURSEVI:v6p331#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p331#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p331#3/r5.claim: They return only to God, through death and then resurrection, and should therefore do what Abraham commanded.
BURSEVI:v6p331#3/r5.anchor: {إليه} لا إلى غيره {ترجعون} تردون بالموت ثم البعث فافعلوا ما أمرتكم به

STUDYQURAN:29:16/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:16/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:29:16/r3.claim: Abraham criticizes his father’s idol worship elsewhere, while his father and people justify it by saying they follow their ancestors.
STUDYQURAN:29:16/r3.anchor: His criticism of their idol worship is found in several accounts, as when he chastises his father, saying, Do you take idols for gods?

STUDYQURAN:29:16/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:16/r4.speaker: IJ
STUDYQURAN:29:16/r4.claim: “Creating perversion” means lying by claiming that the idols are gods.
STUDYQURAN:29:16/r4.anchor: That they only create perversion refers to their lie in claiming that their idols are gods (IJ)

STUDYQURAN:29:16/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:16/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:29:16/r5.claim: The idols cannot provide sustenance, exposing their worship as futile; they are not even lesser intermediaries bringing worshippers near to God, as idolaters claim, and Jesus makes a similar argument.
STUDYQURAN:29:16/r5.anchor: That the idols they worship have no power over what provision may come (cf. 16:73) indicates the utter futility of their worship

STUDYQURAN:29:16/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:29:16/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:29:16/r6.claim: The return to God refers to the Resurrection.
STUDYQURAN:29:16/r6.anchor: speaks to the promise of the Resurrection; see 2:28c.

TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī glosses the idols as likenesses or images worshipped besides God.
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r1.anchor: من دون الله أوثانا، يعني مثلا

TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r2.claim: Qatada explains the idols as statues.
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله " {إنما تعبدون من دون الله أوثانا} [العنكبوت: 17] أصناما "

TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says they manufacture falsehood.
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r3.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: " {وتخلقون إفكا} [العنكبوت: 17] يقول: تصنعون كذبا "

TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r4.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas glosses the phrase as their telling lies.
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، " {وتخلقون إفكا} [العنكبوت: 17] يقول: وتقولون إفكا "

TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، " {وتخلقون إفكا} [العنكبوت: 17] يقول: تقولون كذبا "

TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r6.claim: A report through ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī says Ibn Abbas glossed this as carving and shaping falsehood.
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله " {وتخلقون إفكا} [العنكبوت: 17] قال: تنحتون، تصورون إفكا "

TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r7.claim: Qatada takes the phrase to mean making idols.
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r7.anchor: عن قتادة، " {وتخلقون إفكا} [العنكبوت: 17] أي تصنعون أصناما "

TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the falsehood as the idols they carve with their own hands.
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r8.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " {وتخلقون إفكا} [العنكبوت: 17] الأوثان التي ينحتونها بأيديهم "

TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r9.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers “you fabricate a lie and falsehood,” rather than taking the phrase as merely carving idols.
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r9.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب قول من قال: معناه: وتصنعون كذبا.

TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r10.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r10.claim: He says إفكا is coordinated back to إنما, as in repeating “you only do this.”
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r10.anchor: وإنما في قوله {إفكا} [العنكبوت: 17] مردود على إنما، كقول القائل: إنما تفعلون كذا

TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r11.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r11.claim: Regional readers lighten خ and put ḍamma on ل; al-Ṭabarī accepts this reading because the authoritative readers agree on it.
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r11.anchor: وقرأ جميع قراء الأمصار: {وتخلقون إفكا} [العنكبوت: 17] بتخفيف الخاء من قوله: {وتخلقون} [العنكبوت: 17] وضم اللام

TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r12.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r12.claim: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī is reported to read with fatḥa on خ and a doubled ل, from التخليق.
TAB-FULL:v18p373#2/r12.anchor: وذكر عن أبي عبد الرحمن السلمي أنه قرأ: «وتخلقون إفكا» بفتح الخاء , وتشديد اللام من التخليق.

TAB-FULL:v18p375/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p375/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p375/r1.claim: The idols worshipped besides God have no power to provide their worshippers with anything.
TAB-FULL:v18p375/r1.anchor: على رزقه إياكم، ونعمه التي أنعمها عليكم.

TAB-FULL:v18p375/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p375/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p375/r2.claim: People should seek provision from God rather than their idols, so they may obtain what they seek.
TAB-FULL:v18p375/r2.anchor: على رزقه إياكم، ونعمه التي أنعمها عليكم.

TAB-FULL:v18p375/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p375/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p375/r3.claim: Worship God humbly, recognizing that He provides for and blesses you.
TAB-FULL:v18p375/r3.anchor: على رزقه إياكم، ونعمه التي أنعمها عليكم.

TAB-FULL:v18p375/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p375/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p375/r4.claim: Thank God for His provision and the blessings He has bestowed on you.
TAB-FULL:v18p375/r4.anchor: على رزقه إياكم، ونعمه التي أنعمها عليكم.

TAB-FULL:v18p375/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p375/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p375/r5.claim: Both شكرته and شكرت له mean “I thanked him,” but the latter phrasing is more eloquent.
TAB-FULL:v18p375/r5.anchor: يقال: شكرته وشكرت له، والثانية أفصح من شكرته.

TAB-FULL:v18p375/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p375/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p375/r6.claim: After death people return to God for questioning about worshipping others, despite being His creatures who live on His blessings and eat His provision.
TAB-FULL:v18p375/r6.anchor: وقوله: {إليه ترجعون} [البقرة: 28] يقول: إلى الله تردون من بعد مماتكم

TABATABAI:29:14-17/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:14-17/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:14-17/r12.claim: أوثان is the plural of وثن, meaning an idol.
TABATABAI:29:14-17/r12.anchor: الأوثان جمع وثن بفتحتين وهو الصنم

TABATABAI:29:14-17/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:14-17/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:14-17/r13.claim: إفك is something turned away from its true direction, whether a statement or an act.
TABATABAI:29:14-17/r13.anchor: والإفك الأمر المصروف عن وجهه قولا أو فعلا

TABATABAI:29:14-17/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:14-17/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:14-17/r14.claim: Calling the idols merely idols exposes the falsehood of their worship and makes clear that true worship belongs to God alone; the indefinite plural belittles them as empty claims to divinity.
TABATABAI:29:14-17/r14.anchor: { أوثانا } منكر للدلالة على وهن أمرها وكون ألوهيتها دعوى مجردة لا حقيقة وراءها

TABATABAI:29:17-19/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:17-19/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:17-19/r1.claim: They fabricate falsehood by naming idols gods and worshiping them; a God worthy of worship exists, but He is the one God, not the idols.
TABATABAI:29:17-19/r1.anchor: أي وتفتعلون كذبا بتسميتها آلهة وعبادتها بعد ذلك فهناك إله تجب عبادته لكنه هو الله الواحد

TABATABAI:29:17-19/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:17-19/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:17-19/r2.claim: People worship idols as intermediaries to attract benefit and provision, but idols cannot provide it: God created both people and their provision, and ownership follows creation.
TABATABAI:29:17-19/r2.anchor: إنما تعبدونهم لجلب النفع وهو أن يرضوا عنكم فيرزقوكم ويدروا عليكم الرزق لكنهم ليسوا يملكون لكم رزقا

TABATABAI:29:17-19/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:17-19/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:17-19/r3.claim: Since God alone owns provision, people should seek it from Him, worship Him rather than idols, and thank Him for His many blessings; the benefactor must be thanked.
TABATABAI:29:17-19/r3.anchor: فاطلبوا الرزق من عند الله لأنه هو الذي يملكه فلا تعبدوهم بل اعبدوا الله واشكروا له

TABATABAI:29:17-19/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:29:17-19/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:29:17-19/r4.claim: The return to God explains worship and gratitude, shifting their motive from worldly provision to judgment: natural causes govern provision, but faith and worship determine afterlife happiness.
TABATABAI:29:17-19/r4.anchor: ولذا جيء بالفصل من غير عطف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r1.claim: Abū ʿUbayda distinguishes wooden or stone carvings as awthān, while an idol made from gold, silver, or copper is a ṣanam.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: الأوثان: كل ما كان منحوتا من خشب أو حجر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes the idols here to be those made from stone.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r2.anchor: وهذا كما قال ابن عباس: يريد الأصنام التى تتخذ من الحجارة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r3.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says خلق and اختلق, خرق and اخترق, and افترى all share the sense of fabrication.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: خلق واختلق، وخرق واخترق وافترى؛ واحد كله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r4.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddī takes this as fabricating lies in speech, falsely claiming that idols are gods; Ibn ʿAbbās likewise says they speak lies.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r4.anchor: وفي هذا قولان للمفسرين؛ أحدهما: أن هذا محمول على الكذب في القول. وهو قول السدي؛ قال: تقولون إفكا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also interprets the phrase as speaking lies.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r5.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس: تقولون كذبا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r6.claim: Mujāhid takes the phrase as making idols by hand and naming the things they made gods.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r6.anchor: قال مجاهد: وتصنعون أصناما بأيديكم فتسمونها آلهة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r7.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r7.claim: Al-Kalbī says they make falsehood from sticks and stones with their own hands.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r7.anchor: وقال الكلبي: جعلتم بأيديكم من العيدان والحجارة إفكا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r8.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r8.claim: Qatāda says they make and carve idols.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r9.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r9.claim: Al-Ḥasan glosses the phrase as carving falsehood.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r10.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r10.claim: Muqātil says they make idols with their hands and falsely claim those idols are gods.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r10.anchor: وقال مقاتل: تعملونها بأيديكم، ثم تزعمون أنها آلهة كذبا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r11.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r11.claim: Abū Isḥāq paraphrases this view: they worship idols besides God even though they manufacture them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p505#2/r11.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: ويكون التأويل على هذا القول: إنما تعبدون من دون الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:29:17/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:29:17/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:29:17/r1.claim: They fabricate a lie by claiming that idols are partners of God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:29:17/r1.anchor: أي: تقولون كذبا: إن الأوثان شركاء الله

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p622/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p622/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p622/r4.claim: “You create” means “you make,” and the falsehood is a lie, as in the verse about what people carve.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p622/r4.anchor: إنما تعبدون من دون الله أوثانا وتخلقون} [العنكبوت: 16-17] ، أي: وتصنعون. {إفكا} [العنكبوت: 17] ، يعني: كذبا كقوله: {أتعبدون ما تنحتون} [الصافات: 95]

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p622/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p622/r5.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p622/r5.claim: Mujāhid glosses the phrase as making lies.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p622/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد: قال: {وتخلقون إفكا} [العنكبوت: 17] يقول كذبا.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p622/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p622/r6.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p622/r6.claim: Al-Suddī glosses the phrase as fabricating lies.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p622/r6.anchor: وقال السدي: {وتخلقون إفكا} [العنكبوت: 17] ، يعني: تخرصون كذبا.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p622/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p622/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p622/r7.claim: The idols worshipped besides God cannot provide their worshippers with sustenance.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p622/r7.anchor: قال: {إن الذين تعبدون من دون الله لا يملكون لكم رزقا فابتغوا عند الله الرزق} [العنكبوت: 17] فإن هذه الأوثان لا تملك لكم رزقا.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p623/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p623/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p623/r1.claim: People should seek provision from God by worshipping and thanking Him, and He will provide for them.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p623/r1.anchor: {واعبدوه واشكروا له} [العنكبوت: 17] ، أي: فابتغوا عند الله الرزق بأن تعبدوه وتشكروه يرزقكم.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p623/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p623/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p623/r2.claim: The return to God occurs on Judgment Day.

ELMALILI:29:16-24/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:29:16-24/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:29:16-24/r1.claim: Awthan is the plural of wathan, any object worshipped, including stone images and fetishes; it is broader than asnam and includes standing stones and crosses.
ELMALILI:29:16-24/r1.anchor: “Evsân” müfredi “vesen” taş vesâireden tapılan herhangi bir şey, fetiş ki “esnâm”dan e‘amdır.

ELMALILI:29:16-24/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:29:16-24/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:29:16-24/r2.claim: They fabricate falsehood by calling idols gods or intercessors; the idols are merely imagined entities.

ELMALILI:29:16-24/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:29:16-24/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:29:16-24/r3.claim: A portrait of Zayd contains no reality of the living Zayd, only an image of his mortal body; keeping the image and calling it Zayd is a lie.
ELMALILI:29:16-24/r3.anchor: Meselâ Zeyd’in resminde bile Zeyd’den bir hakikat yoktur. O resim, bir kıymeti olan canlı Zeyd’in değil, nihâyet toprağa gömülecek ölü bedeninin bir hayâlidir.

ELMALILI:29:16-24/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:29:16-24/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:29:16-24/r4.claim: Granting worship to transient imaginings is a grave slander.
ELMALILI:29:16-24/r4.anchor: böyle hayâl olan fânîlere mâbud pâyesi vermek ne büyük bühtandır.

ELMALILI:29:16-24/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:29:16-24/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:29:16-24/r5.claim: Idols cannot provide sustenance; without God's grace they cannot even help someone digest a morsel.
ELMALILI:29:16-24/r5.anchor: Allah’ın inâyeti olmayınca meselâ bir lokmacık hazmettiremezler.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:16/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:16/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:16/r1.claim: Abraham called his people to worship the one God, a principle shared by all prophets, reflect on whether idols truly have divine qualities, and learn from earlier peoples who called their messengers liars.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:29:16/r1.anchor: İbrâhim, öncelikle halkını, bütün peygamberlerin tebliğlerinin ortak ilkesi olan bir Allah’a kul olmaya, tanrı diye taptıkları putların gerçekten tanrı niteliklerine sahip olup olmadıkları üzerinde düşünmeye çağırmış

BAQILLANI:v1p100/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p100/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p100/r1.claim: Some rhetoricians treat interruption and return as a badiʿ figure, while others separate it; poems and Quranic passages show the shift and return in argument or narrative.
BAQILLANI:v1p100/r1.anchor: ومنهم من لا يعد الاعتراض والرجوع من هذا الباب ومنهم من يفرده عنه كقول زهير

BAQILLANI:v1p100/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p100/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p100/r2.claim: Abraham's speech first calls his people to worship and fear God, then directly exposes their idolatry and fabrication before narrating their reply, exemplifying the figure in Quranic discourse.
BAQILLANI:v1p100/r2.anchor: ونظير ذلك من القرآن ما حكى الله تعالى عن إبراهيم الخليل

BURHAN:v2p484/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p484/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p484/r4.claim: When a present tense verb functions like a noun, it takes noun-like inflection, as in the sequence of commands to seek provision, worship, and give thanks.
BURHAN:v2p484/r4.anchor: وإذا جرى المضارع مجرى الاسم أعرب

BURHAN:v2p49/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p49/r4.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
BURHAN:v2p49/r4.claim: Al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr says revelation does not genuinely conflict with itself or reason; because God alone creates, تخلقون means “fabricate a lie” and Jesus’s خلق means “shape” clay.
BURHAN:v2p49/r4.anchor: قال القاضي أبو بكر في ( التقريب ) لا يجوز

BURHAN:v3p322#2/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p322#2/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p322#2/r2.claim: Abraham's rebuke uses direct second-person forms—“you worship” and “you fabricate”—as an instance of shifting from third-person narration to address.
BURHAN:v3p322#2/r2.anchor: إنما تعبدون من دون الله أوثانا وتخلقون إفكا

BURHAN:v4p99/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p99/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p99/r1.claim: The rule that a second definite noun repeats the first applies when repetition is unintended; 29:17 deliberately repeats, as the prior repeated mention of Lord also illustrates.
BURHAN:v4p99/r1.anchor: وهذه القاعدة فيما اذا لم يقصد التكرير وهذه الآية من قصد التكرير ويدل عليه تكرير ذكر الرب فيما قبله

BURHAN:v4p99/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p99/r2.speaker: غيره
BURHAN:v4p99/r2.claim: Another explanation says إله means “the worshipped”; a derived predicate denotes its attribute, so repeating ضارب with different objects does not repeat the same predicate in substance.
BURHAN:v4p99/r2.anchor: واجاب غيره بان اله بمعنى معبود والاسم المشتق انما يقصد به ما تضمنه من الصفة

BURHAN:v4p99/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p99/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p99/r6.claim: The source calls 29:17 a counterexample to the rule that a following definite noun is simply identical with the prior indefinite noun.
BURHAN:v4p99/r6.anchor: لا يملكون لكم رزقا فابتغوا عند الله الرزق

BURHAN:v3p152/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p152/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p152/r1.claim: One reading takes الرزق in the earlier verse to mean one's share or allotment, so no ellipsis needs to be supplied.
BURHAN:v3p152/r1.anchor: وقيل الرزق في الآية الأولى الحظ والنصيب فلا حاجة إلى تقدير

SULAMI:v2p115#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p115#3/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p115#3/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ says to seek provision through obedience and turning toward worship.
SULAMI:v2p115#3/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمة الله عليه : اطلبوا الرزق بالطاعة والإقبال على العبادة

SULAMI:v2p115#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p115#3/r2.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
SULAMI:v2p115#3/r2.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Muʿādh distinguishes four motives for worship: habit, hope for mercy, desire, and love.
SULAMI:v2p115#3/r2.anchor: قال يحيى بن معاذ : يعبدون الله تعالى في الدنيا على أربعة اوجه ، عابد يعبده على العادة وتائب يعبده على الرحمة ومشتاق يعبده على الرغبة وصديق يعبده على المحبة

SULAMI:v2p115#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p115#3/r3.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p115#3/r3.claim: Sahl says to seek provision through trust in God rather than earning, which he calls the way of ordinary people.
SULAMI:v2p115#3/r3.anchor: قال سهل رحمة الله عليه : اطلبوا الرزق في التوكل لا في الكسب فإن طلب الرزق في الكسب سبيل العوام

ITQAN:v2p325#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p325#3/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p325#3/r1.claim: In 29:17, تخلقون means 'make' or 'fashion,' and إفكا means 'a lie'.

ITQAN:v3p80#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p80#2/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق الإسفراييني
ITQAN:v3p80#2/r1.claim: If two verses cannot be reconciled, al-Isfarayini says to establish their chronology and treat the later as abrogating the earlier; if chronology is unknown, consensus on one practice identifies the abrogating verse. He says no unresolved case falls outside these conditions.
ITQAN:v3p80#2/r1.anchor: قال الأستاذ أبو إسحاق الإسفراييني إذا تعارضت الآي وتعذر فيها الترتيب والجمع طلب التاريخ

ITQAN:v3p80#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p80#2/r3.speaker: الصيرفي
ITQAN:v3p80#2/r3.claim: Al-Sayrafi defines real contradiction as mutually opposed meanings in every respect; nothing in Qur'an or Sunna has that defect, while abrogation occurs at different times.
ITQAN:v3p80#2/r3.anchor: وقال الصيرفي جماع الاختلاف والتناقص أن كل كلام صح أن يضاف بعض ما وقع الاسم عليه

ITQAN:v3p80#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p80#2/r4.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
ITQAN:v3p80#2/r4.claim: Al-Qadi Abu Bakr denies conflict between Qur'an, reports, and reason: since only God truly creates, he reads تخلقون إفكا as 'you lie' and تخلق as 'you shape'.
ITQAN:v3p80#2/r4.anchor: وقال القاضي أبو بكر لا يجوز تعارض أي القرآن والآثار وما يوجبه العقل فلذلك لم يجعل

TUSTARI:29:17/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:29:17/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:29:17/r1.claim: Seek provision through trust in God, not earning; seeking it by earning is the way of ordinary people.
TUSTARI:29:17/r1.anchor: اطلبوا الرزق بالتوكل لا بالكسب، فإن طلب الرزق بالكسب طريق العوام

TUSTARI:29:17/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:29:17/r2.speaker: عيسى بن مريم
TUSTARI:29:17/r2.claim: Jesus says people truly desire neither this world nor the next: obedience to the Lord of either would bring it, but they obey neither.
TUSTARI:29:17/r2.anchor: حكي عن عيسى بن مريم عليه السلام أنه قال: بحق أقول لكم

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p9/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p9/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p9/r1.claim: He says people today invent falsehoods out of ignorance and disregard the warning against speaking ignorantly about a verse's occasion of revelation.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p9/r1.anchor: وأما اليوم فكل أحد يخترع شيئا ويختلق إفكا وكذبا ملقيا زمامه إلى الجهالة

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p9/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p9/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p9/r2.claim: This problem prompted his comprehensive book on occasions of revelation, meant to help students find truth, avoid deceit and lies, and preserve reports after hearing and study.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p9/r2.anchor: وذلك الذي حدا بي إلى إملاء هذا الكتاب الجامع للأسباب، لينتهي إليه طالبوا هذا الشأن والمتكلمون في نزول القرآن

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p9/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p9/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p9/r3.claim: The book first treats revelation's beginnings, how the Quran initially descended, and Gabriel's continued delivery in summary, then details every verse with a transmitted occasion when one exists.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p9/r3.anchor: ثم نفرغ للقول مفصلا في سبب نزول كل آية روي لها سبب مقول، مروي منقول

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r4.claim: In these Qur'anic examples, خلق means fabrication and lying; the entry also cites the earlier nations' claim that the message was their custom.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p283/r4.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الخلق في القرآن على ثمانية أوجه

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p337#7/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p337#7/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p337#7/r1.claim: Awthān is the plural of wathan, an idol made from stone or plaster.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p337#7/r1.anchor: (الأوثان) واحدها: وثن. وهو: ما كان من حجارة أو جص.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p337#7/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p337#7/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p337#7/r2.claim: Takhluqūna ifkan means that you fabricate a lie.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p273#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p273#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p273#2/r1.claim: Khalq can mean fabrication or conjectural lying: the source explains the phrases in 26:137 and 29:17 that way and equates ikhtilāq with invented falsehood.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p273#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p273#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p273#2/r2.claim: Khalq also means forming or shaping, as in shaping clay into the likeness of a bird.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p273#2/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p273#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p273#2/r3.claim: Khalq can mean bringing into being or initiating creation.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p273#2/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p273#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p273#2/r4.claim: The underlying sense of khalq is measuring or determining; the leather-cutter shapes what he then cuts, as Zuhayr's verse illustrates.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p273#2/r4.anchor: قال زهير : ولأنت تفري ما خلقت

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p273#2/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p273#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p273#2/r5.claim: Khalq can mean religion: “no change to God's khalq” means no change to God's religion.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p273#2/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p273#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p273#2/r6.claim: The command to alter God's khalq may refer to changing religion, or to bodily practices such as castration and slitting ears.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p273#2/r6.anchor: أي دينه: ويقال: تغيير خلقه بالخصاء

NAHHAS:v3p252/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p252/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p252/r5.claim: In innamā, mā is a particle that blocks inna; it cannot be a relative complement because inna does not govern a verb.
NAHHAS:v3p252/r5.anchor: ما كافة ولا يجوز أن يكون صلة لأن إن لا تقع على الفعل

NAHHAS:v3p252/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p252/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p252/r6.claim: Even when a noun follows, as in innamā Zaydun jālis, mā remains a blocking particle.
NAHHAS:v3p252/r6.anchor: فإن كان بعد ما اسم فقلت إنما زيد جالس فما أيضا كافة

NAHHAS:v3p252/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p252/r7.speaker: بعض النحويين
NAHHAS:v3p252/r7.claim: Some grammarians allow mā to be a relative pronoun, as in innamā Zaydan jālis.
NAHHAS:v3p252/r7.anchor: وأجاز بعض النحويين أن يكون صلة فتقول إنما زيدا جالس

NAHHAS:v3p252/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p252/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p252/r8.claim: Outside the Qur'anic reading, awthānan may be nominative if mā is a relative pronoun, taʿbudūna its clause with an omitted pronoun, and awthānan the predicate of inna.
NAHHAS:v3p252/r8.anchor: ويجوز في غير القرآن رفع أوثان

NAHHAS:v3p252/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p252/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p252/r9.claim: Ifkan is accusative as the direct object of the verb alone.
NAHHAS:v3p252/r9.anchor: فأما ( وتخلقون إفكا ) فهو منصوب بالفعل لا غير

SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r1.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r1.claim: The common reading is from خلق; إفكا means fabricate a lie or carve idols.
SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r1.anchor: العامة بفتح التاء وسكون الخاء وسكون اللام، مضارع خلق، " إفكا " بكسر الهمزة وسكون الفاء أي: وتختلقون كذبا أو تنحتون أصناما.

SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب وزيد بن علي والسلمي وقتادة
SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r2.claim: Ali, Zayd ibn Ali, al-Sulami, and Qatada read with doubled ل, from تخلق; one ت is elided.
SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r2.anchor: وعلي بن أبي طالب وزيد بن علي والسلمي وقتادة

SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r3.speaker: زيد بن علي
SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r3.claim: Zayd ibn Ali is also reported with damma on ت and doubled ل.
SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r3.anchor: وروي عن زيد بن علي أيضا " تخلقون " بضم التاء وتشديد اللام مضارع خلق مضعفا.

SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r4.speaker: ابن الزبير وفضيل بن زرقان
SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r4.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr and Fudayl ibn Zarqan read أفكا as a verbal noun like lying.
SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن الزبير وفضيل بن زرقان " أفكا " بفتح الهمزة وكسر الفاء وهو مصدر كالكذب معنى ووزنا.

SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows إفك to be shortened from أفك or an adjective meaning false creation.
SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r5.anchor: وجوز الزمخشري في الإفك بالكسر والسكون وجهين، أحدهما: أن يكون مخففا من الأفك بالفتح والكسر كالكذب واللعب،

SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r6.claim: Al-Samin says an omitted noun is unnecessary if إفك is an adjective; it is needed only as a verbal noun.
SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r6.anchor: قلت: وتقديره مضافا قبل إفك مع جعله له صفة غير محتاج إليه، وإنما كان يحتاج إليه لو جعله مصدرا.

SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r7.claim: رزقا is an accusative verbal noun governed by لا يملكون.
SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r7.anchor: يجوز أن يكون منصوبا على المصدر، وناصبه " لا يملكون " لأنه في معناه.

SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r8.speaker: أصول الكوفيين
SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r8.claim: Kufan analysis supplies لا يملكون أن يرزقوكم رزقا, with the infinitive clause as object.
SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r8.anchor: وعلى أصول الكوفيين يجوز أن يكون الأصل: لا يملكون أن يرزقوكم رزقا، ف " أن يرزقوكم " هو مفعول " يملكون ".

SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r9.claim: Alternatively رزقا means that which is provided and is a direct object.
SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r9.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون بمعنى المرزوق، فينتصب مفعولا به.

ZAJJAJ:v4p164/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p164/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p164/r4.claim: A recitation is reported with the form وَتَخْلُقُونَ إِفْكًا.
ZAJJAJ:v4p164/r4.anchor: من دون الله أوثانا وتخلقون إفكا

ZAJJAJ:v4p164/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p164/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p164/r6.claim: One explanation is that they invent lies.
ZAJJAJ:v4p164/r6.anchor: وتخلقون إفكا فيه قولان: تخلقون كذبا

ZAJJAJ:v4p164/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p164/r7.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v4p164/r7.claim: Another explanation is that they manufacture the idols they worship.
ZAJJAJ:v4p164/r7.anchor: وقيل تعملون الأصنام، ويكون التأويل على هذا

ASAD-NOTES:29:16#n13/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:29:16#n13/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:29:16#n13/r1.claim: The literal wording is 'you create a lie.'

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p402/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p402/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p402/r1.claim: Arabic khalaqa begins with the sense of measuring or shaping; attributed to God it means originating without precedent, while khalaqa al-kalām means composing speech and ikhtalaqa means fabricating it.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p402/r1.anchor: الخَلْق في معجم العربية: التقدير. فإذا أسند إلى الخالق، فهو إبداع الشيء على غير مثال سبق. وخلق الكلام: صنعه: واختلقه: افتراه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p402/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p402/r2.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p402/r2.claim: Al-Rāghib reserves creation in the sense of origination to God; when humans are said to create speech, it means falsehood, which is why many objected to calling the Qurʾān created.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p402/r2.anchor: وقال "الراغب": الخَلْق التقدير المستقيم، واستعمل في إبداع الشيء من غير أصل ولا احتذاء

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p402/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p402/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p402/r3.claim: Bint maps the wider root family: khulq appears in al-Shuʿarāʾ 137 and al-Qalam 4, ikhtilāq in Ṣād 7, and khalaqa forms roughly 250 times; khallāq and mukhallaqa each occur twice.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p160/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p160/r1.speaker: السلمي وزيد بن علي
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p160/r1.claim: Al-Sulamī and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read وتخلقون إفكا; Ibn Jinnī says تخلقون follows the pattern and meaning of تكذبون, fabricating falsehood.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p160/r1.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة السلمى وزيد بن علي: "وتخلقون إفكا"

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p160/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p160/r2.speaker: فضيل بن مرزوق وابن الزبير
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p160/r2.claim: Fuḍayl ibn Marzūq and Ibn al-Zubayr read أفكا with open hamza; Ibn Jinnī analyzes it as either a verbal noun or an adjective replacing an omitted noun, and also allows a shortened active participle of آفك.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p160/r2.anchor: وقرأ فضيل بن مرزوق6 وابن الزبير

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p160/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p160/r3.speaker: الزهري
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p160/r3.claim: Al-Zuhrī reads يبدا without a fully articulated hamza; Ibn Jinnī says it is softened, not replaced outright, since true replacement would yield yāʾ and then alif, as in Abu Zayd’s poetic ملا for ملأ.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p160/r3.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة الزهري: "أولم يروا كيف يبدا الله الخلق"

QIRAAT-ER:29:17:31#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:29:17:31#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:29:17:31#1/r1.claim: The active reading means you return rather than you are returned, giving the addressees agency in their return.
QIRAAT-ER:29:17:31#1/r1.anchor: Active voice reading: ""you return"" instead of passive ""you are returned"" — grants agency to the addressees

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p96#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p96#2/r1.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p96#2/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan glosses “you create a falsehood” as “you carve a falsehood,” referring to making idols.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p96#2/r1.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله ﴿ وتخلقون إفكا ﴾ قال تنحتون إفكا

ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r1.claim: The restriction says they worship only idols, man-made statues with no quality beyond being fashioned, showing their religion is false in itself as well as against true religion.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r1.anchor: بيان لبطلان دينهم وشريته في نفسه بعد بيان شريته بالنسبة إلى الدين الحق

ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r2.claim: One explanation is that they lie by calling the statues gods and claiming they intercede; another takes the phrase as making them for falsehood, with the lām marking an outcome rather than intent.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r2.anchor: أي وتكذبون كذبا حيث تسمونها آلهة وتدعون أنها شفعاؤكم عند الله سبحانه أو تعملونها وتنحتونها للافك والكذب

ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r3.claim: A further possibility is that the wording is sarcastic.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r3.anchor: وجوز أن يكون ذلك من باب التهكم

ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r4.speaker: بعض الأفاضل
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r4.claim: Another scholar takes إفكا as the idols themselves, calling them falsehood by hyperbole, or as something turned from its proper state because people treat manufactured idols as creators.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r4.anchor: وقال بعض الأفاضل : الأظهر كون إفكا مفعولا به والمراد به نفس الاوثان

ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r5.speaker: علي والسلمي وعون العقيلي وعبادة وابن أبي ليلى وزيد بن علي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r5.claim: These readers pronounce the verb with an open initial tā and geminated lām; Ibn Mujahid traces it to تتخلقون, with one tā dropped, meaning to fabricate a lie emphatically.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه والسلمي وعون العقيلي وعبادة وابن أبي ليلى وزيد بن علي

ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r6.speaker: ابن مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r6.claim: Ibn Mujahid says this reading is also transmitted from Ibn al-Zubayr; some allow the form to carry the basic meaning فعل.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r6.anchor: قال ابن مجاهد : ورويت عن ابن الزبير وأصله تتخلقون

ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r7.speaker: زيد بن علي
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r7.claim: Zayd ibn Ali also has a reading from خلق with a geminated lām, describing repeated making in the sense of lying and slander.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي رضي الله تعالى عنهما أيضا ( تخلقون ) من خلق بالتشديد

ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r8.speaker: ابن الزبير وفضيل بن زرقان
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r8.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr and Fudayl ibn Zarqan read إفكا with fatḥa on the hamza and kasra on fā, as a verbal noun or adjective modifying an omitted description of their fabrication.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن الزبير وفضيلوفضيل بن زرقان ( إفكا ) بفتح الهمزة وكسر الفاء

ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r9.claim: The idols are worthless because they cannot benefit their worshippers: they cannot provide any sustenance, whether رزقا means the act of providing or what is provided.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r9.anchor: أي لا يستطيعون إيتاء شيء من الرزق

ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r10.claim: If رزقا is a verbal noun, it may be an absolute object by meaning or depend on an omitted verb, though Alusi considers the latter analysis strained.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r10.anchor: وجوز على المصدرية أن يكون مفعولا مطلقا ليملكون من معناه أو لمحذوف والأصل لا يملكون أن يرزقوكم رزقا وهو كما ترى

ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r11.speaker: بعض الأجلة
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r11.claim: One eminent scholar says the indefinite رزقا intensifies the negation by suggesting even a little sustenance is beyond the idols; provision is singled out for its importance in creation.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r11.anchor: وقال بعض الاجلة : للتحقير والتقليل مبالغة في النفي وخص الرزق لمكانته من الخلق

ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r12.claim: They should seek all provision from God; the repeated definite noun may be all-encompassing rather than identical to the earlier indefinite رزقا.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r12.anchor: أي كله على أن تعريف الرزق للاستغراق قال الطيبي هذا من المواضع التي ليست المعرفة المعادة عين الاول فيها

ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r13.claim: They should worship God alone and thank Him for His blessings, using worship to seek their needs and gratitude to retain blessings and obtain more.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r13.anchor: على نعمائه متوسلين إلى مطالبكم بعبادته مقيدين بشكره تعالى للعتيد ومستجلبين به للمزيد

ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r14.claim: The two imperatives may continue the preceding argument about provision or anticipate the return to God by preparing for the meeting through worship and thanks.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r14.anchor: وجوز أن يكونا ناظرتين لقوله تعالى : ( إليه ترجعون

ALUSI-FULL:v20p145/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p145/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p145/r1.claim: The return clause may conclude everything Abraham said or its opening; the only return is to God at death and resurrection, so the people should obey, with the intervening case against idols as a parenthesis.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p145/r1.anchor: أن تكون هذه الجملة تذييلا لجملة ما سبق مما حكي عن إبراهيم عليه السلام أو لأوله والمعنى اليه تعالى لا إلى غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v20p145/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p145/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p145/r2.claim: A reading with fatḥa on tā takes the verb from رجع, meaning that the people themselves return.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p145/r2.anchor: وقريء ( ترجعون ) بفتح التاء من رجع رجوعا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p236#3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p236#3/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p236#3/r1.claim: The objects worshipped apart from God are idols.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p236#3/r1.anchor: {إنما تعبدون من دون الله أوثانا} أصناما،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p236#3/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p236#3/r2.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p236#3/r2.claim: Mujahid explains that they make idols with their hands and then call them gods.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p236#3/r2.anchor: قال مجاهد: تصنعون أصناما بأيدكم فتسمونها آلهة،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p236#3/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p236#3/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p236#3/r3.claim: The idols cannot provide people with sustenance; people should seek provision from God, worship Him, thank Him, and return to Him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p236#3/r3.anchor: لا يقدرون أن يرزقوكم، {فابتغوا} فاطلبوا، {عند الله الرزق واعبدوه واشكروا له

BAYDAWI-FULL:29:16-17/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:16-17/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:16-17/r4.claim: They worship idols and fabricate claims by calling them gods and alleging that they intercede with God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:16-17/r4.anchor: وتكذبون كذبا في تسميتها آلهة وادعاء شفاعتها عند الله تعالى

BAYDAWI-FULL:29:16-17/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:16-17/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:16-17/r5.claim: Alternatively, they make and carve the idols for the sake of falsehood; the phrase shows their practice is vile because it is fraud and untruth.
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:16-17/r5.anchor: أو تعملونها وتنحتونها للإفك وهو استدلال على شرارة ما هم عليه

BAYDAWI-FULL:29:16-17/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:16-17/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:16-17/r6.claim: Readings include form II, suggesting repeated making, and form V, suggesting affected or pretended making.
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:16-17/r6.anchor: وقرىء »تخلقون« من خلق للتكثير »وتخلقون« من تخلق للتكلف

BAYDAWI-FULL:29:16-17/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:16-17/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:16-17/r7.claim: إفكًا may be a verbal noun like الكذب or an adjective meaning a creation laden with falsehood.
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:16-17/r7.anchor: و { إفكا } على أنه مصدر كالكذب أو نعت بمعنى

BAYDAWI-FULL:29:17-18/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:17-18/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:17-18/r1.claim: This is a second argument against the idols: they cannot bring any benefit by providing sustenance.
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:17-18/r1.anchor: دليل ثان على شرارة ذلك من حيث إنه لا يجدي بطائل

BAYDAWI-FULL:29:17-18/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:17-18/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:17-18/r2.claim: رزقًا may be an infinitive, meaning they cannot provide, or the thing provided; its indefinite form is general.
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:17-18/r2.anchor: يحتمل المصدر بمعنى لا يستطيعون أن يرزقوكم

BAYDAWI-FULL:29:17-18/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:17-18/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:17-18/r3.claim: Seek all sustenance from God, since He owns it.

BAYDAWI-FULL:29:17-18/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:17-18/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:17-18/r4.claim: Worship and gratitude are means to obtain what you need and a way to acknowledge the blessings you have received.
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:17-18/r4.anchor: متوسلين إلى مطالبكم بعبادته مقيدين لما حفكم من النعم بشكره

BAYDAWI-FULL:29:17-18/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:17-18/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:17-18/r5.claim: Alternatively, worship and gratitude prepare people to meet God.

BAYDAWI-FULL:29:17-18/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:17-18/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:29:17-18/r6.claim: A reading has fatḥ on the tāʾ in ترجعون.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p543/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p543/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p543/r14.claim: The phrase sets worship of God apart from worship of idols and describes God as incomparable, with no equal, second, or minister.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p543/r14.anchor: إنما تعبدون } ولما كان الله أعلى من كل شيء قال : { من دون الله } أي الذي لا شبيه له ولا نظير

BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r1.claim: The plural idols scatter attention among many objects of worship; multiplicity entails division, in which there is no good.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r1.anchor: وقال : { أوثانا } إشارة إلى تفرق الهم بكثرة المعبود , والكثرة يلزمها الفرقة ولا خير في الفرقة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r2.claim: Across its permutations, the root وثن conveys increase and multiplicity, then division and softness or weakness; these senses are unfit for divinity.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r2.anchor: ومادة ( وثن ) بجميع تقاليبها وزاوية ويائية ومهموزة تدور على الزيادة والكثرة , ويلزمها الفرقة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r3.claim: Arabic derivatives illustrate abundance, dispersal, and weakness: wealth grows or increases, reports spread, and the fixed thing persists through lack of power to move.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r3.anchor: واستوثن المال : سمن , فزاد لحمه , واستوثن من المال : استكثر , والنحل : صارت فرقتين

BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r4.speaker: أبو منصور
BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r4.claim: Abu Mansur distinguishes a wathn, a bodily object carved and set up for worship, from a sanam, an image without a body; al-Qazzaz transmits the distinction.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r4.anchor: قال أبو منصور : الفرق بين الوثن والصنم أن الوثن كل ما كان له جثة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r5.speaker: بعضهم
BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r5.claim: Some lexicographers instead treat wathn as synonymous with sanam.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r6.speaker: ابن عرفة
BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r6.claim: Ibn Arafa, quoted through al-Harawi by Abd al-Haqq, calls any image made of plaster, stone, or similar material a wathn.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r6.anchor: قال عبد الحق : قال الهروي : قال ابن عرفة : ما كان له صورة من جص أو حجارة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r7.speaker: أبو حاتم أحمد بن حمدان الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r7.claim: Abu Hatim defines a sanam as a stone statue and says a human image made on a wall is also called a wathn.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r7.anchor: قال أبو حاتم أحمد بن حمدان الرازي في كتاب الزينة : الصنم تمثال من حجارة صوروا في الحائط

BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r8.speaker: أبو حاتم أحمد بن حمدان الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r8.claim: Abu Hatim notes that Christians make images of Christ and Mary in their churches and prostrate to them.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r8.anchor: والنصارى يفعلون ذلك ويصورون في بيعهم صورة المسيح وصورة مريم ويسجدون لها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r1.claim: The idols' multiplicity, division, and weakness make them unfit for divine rank, so the verse uses restriction as a reversal of the polytheists' claim that they are gods.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r1.anchor: فقد تحرر أن المادة كلها دائرة على ما لا ينبغي لرتبة الإلهية من الكثرة والفرقة والرخاوة , ولذلك أتى بصيغة الحصر , وهو قصر قلب

BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r2.claim: The present tense points to idol images being continually remade; people falsely call their handmade artifact a creator, a created thing a lord, and a servant an object of worship.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r2.anchor: بصيغة المضارع إشارة إلى ما يرى في كل وقت من تجدد حدوثها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r3.claim: Ifk is something turned away from its proper truth: the fabricated objects are falsely declared divine.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r3.anchor: إفكا } أي شيئا مصروفا عن وجهه , فإنه مصنوع وأنتم تسمونه باسم الصانع

BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r4.claim: Because humans always need benefit, the idols' inability to provide proves that all good belongs to God and that He alone deserves worship, refuting imagined power to benefit or harm.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r4.anchor: صرح بعجزها , وأثبت اختصاصه بالخير , لينتج اسحقاقه للعبادة دونها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r5.claim: The form of ابتغاء suggests exertion: God usually grants provision through effort, whether worship and reliance or ordinary worldly means; the idle should not merely indulge wishes and presume on God.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r5.anchor: وأشار بصيغة الافتعال إلى السعي فيه , لأنه أجرى عادته سبحلنه أنه في الغالب لا يؤتيه إلا بكد من المرزوق وجهد

BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r6.claim: All provision is with God; created things are ordered and interconnected so that removing any part would disorder the whole system.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r6.anchor: الرزق } اي كله , فغنه لا شيء منه إلا وهو بيده , وقد دخل فيه كل موجود , فإن الكل خلق لذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r7.claim: Worship must be sincere and free of association; God alone merits it, rewards the worshipper, and punishes the one who turns away.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r7.anchor: واعْبدوه } اي عبادة يبلهان وهي ما كان خالصا عن الشرك , فإن من يكون كذلك يستحق ذلك ويثيب العابد له

BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r8.claim: Do not let outward earning distract from worship, the true means; a sin may cause a servant to lose provision.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r8.anchor: فلا يشغلكم ابتغاء الرزق بالأسباب الظاهرة عن عبادته , فإنها هي الأسباب الحقيقية , فربما حرم العبد الرزق بالذنب

BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r9.claim: Give thanks to God alone for the blessings He has bestowed.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r9.anchor: واشكروا } اي اوقعوا الشكر { له } خاصة على ما أفاض عليكم من النعم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r10.claim: All true authority belongs to God in this life, and people physically return after death for judgment; He can resurrect them effortlessly and reward or punish them in both abodes.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r10.anchor: إليه } أي وحده { ترجعون * } اي معنى في الدنيا والآخرة بأنه لا حكم في الحقيقة لأحد سواه , وحسا بالنشر والحشر بعد الموت

DURR-FULL:v6p457/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p457/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p457/r1.claim: Qatada says the objects worshipped apart from God are idols.
DURR-FULL:v6p457/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {إنما تعبدون من دون الله أوثانا} قال: أصناما

DURR-FULL:v6p457/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p457/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p457/r2.claim: Qatada explains that the people fabricate falsehood by making idols.
DURR-FULL:v6p457/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {إنما تعبدون من دون الله أوثانا} قال: أصناما {وتخلقون إفكا} قال: تصنعون أصناما

DURR-FULL:v6p457/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p457/r3.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v6p457/r3.claim: Al-Hasan glosses the phrase as carving idols.
DURR-FULL:v6p457/r3.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله {وتخلقون إفكا} قال: تنحتون

DURR-FULL:v6p457/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p457/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p457/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the phrase as making falsehood.
DURR-FULL:v6p457/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وتخلقون إفكا} قال: تصنعون كذبا

DURR-FULL:v6p457/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p457/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p457/r5.claim: Mujahid gives the same explanation as Ibn Abbas: they make falsehood.

DURR-FULL:v6p457/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p457/r15.speaker: عاصم بن أبي النجود
DURR-FULL:v6p457/r15.claim: Asim reads the two letters of afkan lightly and reads awthānan mawaddatan in the accusative with tanwin, with baynakum accusative.
DURR-FULL:v6p457/r15.anchor: عن عاصم بن أبي النجود رضي الله عنه أنه قرأ {وتخلقون افكا} خفيفتين وقرأ {اوثانا مودة} منصوبة منونة {بينكم} نصب

DURR-FULL:v6p457/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p457/r16.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v6p457/r16.claim: Asked about a sick person's praying on a staff, Ibn Umar rejects treating anything as an idol and says to pray standing if able, otherwise sitting, otherwise lying down.
DURR-FULL:v6p457/r16.anchor: سألت ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما عن صلاة المريض على العود قال: لا آمركم أن تتخذوا من دون الله أوثانا

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : اوثانا اي اصناما .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the phrase as putting or fabricating falsehood; Qatada is reported to give the same gloss.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : وتخلقون افكا يقول : وتضعون . وروى عن قتادة مثل ذلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r3.claim: Another reported gloss from Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi is that they say or utter falsehood.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : وتخلقون افكا قال : يقولون افكا . وروى ، عن السدي مثل ذلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r4.speaker: أبوه
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r4.claim: Uthman ibn Ata's father explains the phrase as fashioning or shaping falsehood.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r4.anchor: عن أبيه وتخلقون افكا قال : وتصورون افكا .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r5.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، الحسن، عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan, and Ikrima gloss the phrase as setting up lies.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : وتخلقوا افكا يقول : وتضعون كذبا ، وروي عن مجاهد ، والحسن ، وعكرمة ، مثل ذلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r6.claim: In another gloss, Qatada says they fashion idols.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r6.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : وتخلقون افكا اي تضعون اصناما .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r7.claim: Qatada says the objects worshipped besides God are this idol and this stone.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r7.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : ان الذين تعبدون من دون الله هذا الوثن وهذا الحجر .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r8.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r8.claim: Qatada calls this an honor God bestowed on them and says they should thank Him for His blessings.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r8.anchor: عن قتادة قال : كرامة اكرمكم الله بها ، فاشكروا لله نعمه .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r9.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r9.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi says every deed performed for God counts as gratitude for God's blessings.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p3043#3/r9.anchor: سمعت محمد بن كعب القرظي وهو يقول : ان كل عمل عمل لله فهو شكر لانعم الله .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r1.claim: Exegetes often searched for occasions of revelation, events said to prompt a verse to explain a ruling, narrate an event, condemn it, or serve another purpose.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r1.anchor: وهي حوادث يروى أن آيات من القرآن نزلت لأجلها لبيان حكمها أو لحكايتها أو إنكارها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r2.claim: Some exegetes overdid this search until readers could think every Quranic verse descended in response to a particular event, weakening confidence in their accounts.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r2.anchor: وأغربوا في ذلك وأكثروا حتى كاد بعضهم أن يوهم الناس أن كل آية من القرآن نزلت على سبب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r3.claim: Some verses themselves point to their occasion, and some occasions are established through transmission rather than a narrator’s conjecture; ignoring the topic entirely also risks misunderstanding.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r3.anchor: نجد في بعض آي القرآن إشارة إلى الأسباب التي دعت إلى نزولها ونجد لبعض الآي أسبابا ثبتت بالنقل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r4.claim: Ibn Ashur discusses occasions of revelation in his introduction to assess them carefully during exegesis and avoid repeating the methodological discussion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r4.anchor: فذلك الذي دعاني إلى خوض هذا الغرض في مقدمات التفسير لظهور شدة الحاجة إلى تمحيصه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r5.claim: He excuses early authors who collected many occasions because enthusiasm for a new subject naturally led them to expand their compilations.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r5.anchor: وأنا عاذر المتقدمين الذين ألفوا في أسباب النزول فاستكثروا منها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r6.claim: He does not excuse leading exegetes who accepted weak reports without marking their reliability, creating the false impression that revelation depended on triggering events.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r6.anchor: ولكني لا أعذر أساطين المفسرين الذين تلقفوا الروايات الضعيفة فأثبتوها في كتبهم ولم ينبهوا على مراتبها قوة وضعفا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r7.claim: The Quran guides people toward communal well-being and does not need events to occur before it can reveal legislation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r7.anchor: فإن القرآن جاء هاديا إلى ما به صلاح الأمة في أصناف الصلاح فلا يتوقف نزوله على حدوث الحوادث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r8.claim: Most scholars say an occasion of revelation does not restrict a verse’s general wording; a deviant minority claimed that it does.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r9.claim: The usul principle is that general wording governs rather than the specific occasion, though some reports try to specify general wording or restrict an unrestricted expression and can distort interpretation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r9.anchor: العبرة بعموم اللفظ لا بخصوص السبب ولكن أسبابا كثيرة رام رواتها تعيين مراد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r10.speaker: الواحدي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r10.claim: Al-Wahidi warns that people now invent occasions of revelation and fabricate lies; he says such claims require reports heard from eyewitnesses of revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r10.anchor: الواحدي في أول كتابه في أسباب النزول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r5.speaker: ابن الزبير وفضيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r5.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr and Fuḍayl read “ifkan” on the fiʿl pattern, a verbal noun like lying and laughter.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن الزبير وفضيل «إفكا» على وزن فعل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says “you fashion falsehood” means making idols, named falsehood because people falsely claim they are gods.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r6.anchor: فقال ابن عباس هو نحت الأصنام وخلقها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r7.claim: Mujahid says they fabricate lies about idols and other matters.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هو اختلاق الكذب في أمر الأوثان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r8.speaker: عبد الرحمن السلمي وعون العقيلي وقتادة وابن أبي ليلى
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r8.claim: These readers use the doubled-lām form “wa-takhallaqūna ifkan”; in this reading “ifk” means a lie.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ عبد الرحمن السلمي وعون العقيلي وقتادة وابن أبي ليلى «وتخلقون إفكا»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r9.claim: Abraham argues from provision, familiar to all: idols cannot provide, so seek good from God; provision is singled out for its importance and stands for the whole category.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r9.anchor: ثم وقفهم على جهة الاحتجاج عليهم بأمر تفهمه عامتهم وخاصتهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r10.claim: Provision is central to created life, and one part can signify its entire kind.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r10.anchor: فهو جزء يدل على جنسه كله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r11.claim: “I thanked for you” and “I thanked you” are equivalent Arabic expressions.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r11.anchor: ويقال شكرت لك وشكرتك بمعنى واحد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p310#2/r12.claim: Abraham concludes by informing them of the resurrection and return to God.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p264/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p264/r1.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p264/r1.claim: Al-Farra says إنما here is one particle, not relative ‘that which’; وتخلقون is coordinated with it, as in the cited idiom.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p264/r1.anchor: قال الفراء إنما في هذا الموضع حرف واحد وليست على معنى الذي وقوله وتخلقون إفكا مردود على إنما

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p264/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p264/r3.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p264/r3.claim: Ibn Qutayba says the singular wathan is an object of stone or plaster.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p264/r3.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة واحدها وثن وهو ما كان من حجارة أو جص

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p264/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p264/r4.speaker: ابن السميفع وأبو المتوكل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p264/r4.claim: Ibn al-Sumayfiʿ and Abu al-Mutawakkil read تختلقون, adding a ta.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p264/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن السميفع وأبو المتوكل وتختلقون بزيادة تاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p264/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p264/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p264/r5.claim: One view says they invent the lie that their idols are gods.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p264/r5.anchor: أحدهما تختلقون كذبا في زعمكم أنها آلهة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p264/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p264/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p264/r6.claim: Another says they manufacture the idols they worship.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p264/r6.anchor: والثاني تصنعون الأصنام والمعنى تعبدون أصناما أنتم تصنعونها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p264/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p264/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p264/r7.anchor: أي لا يقدرون على أن يرزقوكم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p264/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p264/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p264/r8.claim: Seek provision from God, who alone can provide it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p264/r8.anchor: أي فاطلبوا من الله فانه القادر على ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r1.claim: Abraham, the exemplar of the hanifs, calls his people to worship God alone, fear Him, seek provision only from Him, and thank Him as the sole giver of blessings; this brings good and repels harm in both lives.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r1.anchor: دعا قومه إلى عبادة الله وحده لا شريك له، والإخلاص له في التقوى، وطلب الرزق منه وحده لا شريك له، وتوحيده في الشكر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r3.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس، مجاهد، السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r3.claim: They say the people invented names for idols as gods, although the idols are created beings like their worshippers and can neither harm nor benefit.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r3.anchor: هكذا روى العوفي عن ابن عباس. وبه قال مجاهد، والسدي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r4.speaker: ابن عباس من رواية الوالبي، مجاهد، عكرمة، الحسن، قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r4.claim: These authorities understand the phrase as making idols by carving them; Ibn Jarir also chooses this interpretation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r4.anchor: وروى الوالبي (6) ، عن ابن عباس: وتصنعون إفكا، أي: تنحتونها أصناما

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r5.claim: The phrase seek provision at God's presence forcefully restricts the request to Him, as in 1:5 and 66:11; no other being controls provision.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r5.anchor: وهذا أبلغ في الحصر، كقوله: {إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r6.claim: Ask God alone for provision; no one else owns anything to give.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r6.anchor: أي: فاطلبوا {عند الله الرزق} أي: لا عند غيره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r7.claim: Eat from God's provision, worship Him alone, and thank Him for His gifts; all will return to Him for judgment and recompense.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r7.anchor: كلوا من رزقه واعبدوه وحده (7) ، واشكروا له على ما أنعم به عليكم، {إليه ترجعون} أي: يوم القيامة، فيجازي كل عامل بعمله

JISHUMI:v8p5553/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5553/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5553/r6.claim: Idols cannot provide sustenance, so people should seek provision from God, worship Him, thank Him, and remember their return to Him.
JISHUMI:v8p5553/r6.anchor: إن الذين تعبدون من دون الله لا يملكون لكم رزقا فابتغوا عند الله الرزق واعبدوه واشكروا له

JISHUMI:v8p5553/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5553/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5553/r7.claim: Their worshippers fabricate lies by inventing false claims about the idols.
JISHUMI:v8p5553/r7.anchor: إنما تعبدون من دون الله أوثانا وتخلقون إفكا

JISHUMI:v8p5553/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5553/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5553/r10.claim: Ifk means a lie; balāgh is conveying a meaning to the mind so it can be understood.
JISHUMI:v8p5553/r10.anchor: الإفك: الكذب. والبلاغ: إلقاء المعنى إلى النفس على سبيل الإفهام.

JISHUMI:v8p5553/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5553/r14.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5553/r14.claim: One analysis takes ما as a particle that makes إنما restrictive, leaving أوثانا accusative as the object.
JISHUMI:v8p5553/r14.anchor: و (ما) في قوله: إنما تعبدون قيل: (ما) الكافة، وقيل: (ما): الذي

JISHUMI:v8p5553/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5553/r15.speaker: علي بن عيسى
JISHUMI:v8p5553/r15.claim: Ali ibn ʿIsa rejects the relative reading of ما: if it meant “that which,” أوثان should be nominative rather than accusative.
JISHUMI:v8p5553/r15.anchor: وليس كذلك؛ إذ لو كان كذلك لقال: أوثان لا (أوثانا)، عن علي بن عيسى.

JISHUMI:v8p5553/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5553/r16.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p5553/r16.claim: If ما is relative, idols are nominative and ما is the object of إن; if إنما is one particle, أوثانا is its accusative object.
JISHUMI:v8p5553/r16.anchor: وقيل: إنه (ما) الذي، فإن حمل على معنى الذي ف (الأوثان) في محل الرفع وتكون (ما) مفعولا من (إن)

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r5.claim: A reading from خَلَقَ gives the sense of multiplying acts of creation; تخلقون from تخلّق means lying and inventing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r5.anchor: وقرىء : ( تخلقون من خلق ) بمعنى التكثير في خلق . وتخلقون ، من تخلق بمعنى تكذب وتخرص .

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r6.claim: إفك can be a verbal noun like كذب and لعب, or an adjective on the faʿl pattern meaning something false and vain.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r6.anchor: وقرىء : ( إفكا ) ، فيه وجهان : أن يكون مصدرا ، نحو : كذب ولعب . والإفك : مخفف منه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r7.claim: Their fabrication may be calling idols gods, partners, or intercessors with God; alternatively idols are lies, and carving them is making falsehood.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r7.anchor: واختلاقهم الإفك : تسميتهم الأوثان آلهة وشركاء الله أو شفعاء إليه . أو سمي الأصنام : إفكا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r8.claim: The indefinite رزقا means idols cannot provide any provision, while the definite الرزق means seek all provision from God, the sole provider.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r8.anchor: لأنه أراد لا يستطيعون أن يرزقوكم شيئا من الرزق ، فابتغوا عند الله الرزق كله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r9.claim: The verb is also read with fatḥa on tāʾ; this calls people to prepare for meeting God through worship and gratitude.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p451/r9.anchor: وقرىء : بفتح التاء ، فاستعدوا للقائه بعبادته والشكر له على أنعمه

MUJAHID:v2p494#4/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p494#4/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p494#4/r1.claim: Mujahid explains “you fabricate falsehood” as “you tell lies.”
MUJAHID:v2p494#4/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ وتخلقون إفكا ﴾ قال تقولون كذبا

MUQATIL:29:16-17/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:29:16-17/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:29:16-17/r3.claim: They fabricate a lie by making and sculpting idols by hand, then claiming these objects are gods; 37:96 says God created them and what they make.
MUQATIL:29:16-17/r3.anchor: ثم تزعمون أنها آلهة كذبا وأنتم تنحتونها

MUQATIL:29:16-17/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:29:16-17/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:29:16-17/r4.claim: The idols cannot provide sustenance, so people should seek provision from God and worship Him by affirming His oneness.
MUQATIL:29:16-17/r4.anchor: ن يقول: لا يقدرون { لكم رزقا } ، على رزق

MUQATIL:29:16-17/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:29:16-17/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:29:16-17/r5.claim: People should thank God for His blessings because they return to Him alive after death.
MUQATIL:29:16-17/r5.anchor: واشكروا الله فى النعم، فإن مصيركم إليه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r1.anchor: ﴿ إنما تعبدون من دون الله أوثانا ﴾ أصناما

NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r2.claim: Takhluqūn can mean that they lie and fabricate, or that they make things.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r3.speaker: أبو حذيفة والسلمى
NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r3.claim: Abu Hudhayfa and al-Sulami read the form from khalaqa, conveying multiplying or making abundantly.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو حذيفة والسلمى رضي الله عنهما وتخلقون من خلق بمعنى التكثير في خلق

NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r4.claim: Afkan is also read; it is a verbal noun like lying or playing, while ifk is its shortened form, as kadhib and laʿib are shortened from their roots.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r4.anchor: وقرىء أفكا وهو مصدر نحو كذب ولعب والافك مخفف منه كالكذب واللعب من أصلهما

NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r5.claim: Their fabrication is calling idols gods and partners of God.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r5.anchor: واختلافهم الافك تسميتهم الأوثان آلهة وشركاء لله

NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r6.claim: The idols cannot provide their worshippers any sustenance; God alone is the provider, so they should seek provision from Him.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r6.anchor: لا يستطيعون أن يرزقوكم شيئا من الرزق

NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r7.claim: Worship and thank God for His blessings, preparing to meet Him, since you will return to Him.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r7.anchor: فاستعدوا للقائه بعبادته والشكر له على أنعمه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r8.speaker: يعقوب
NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r8.claim: Yaqub reads the t with fatḥa and the jīm with kasra, an active form meaning 'you return.'

QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r8.claim: Abu ʿUbayda distinguishes ṣanam, made of gold, silver, or copper, from wathan, made of plaster or stone.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r8.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: الصنم ما يتخذ من ذهب أو من فضة أو نحاس

QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r9.speaker: الجوهري
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r9.claim: Al-Jawhari says wathan means ṣanam and gives its plural as awthān.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r9.anchor: الجوهري: الوثن الصنم والجمع وثن وأوثان

QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r10.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r10.claim: Al-Hasan reads takhluqūn as carving: they worship idols that they themselves manufacture.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r10.anchor: قال الحسن: معنى: { تخلقون } تنحتون فالمعنى

QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r11.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r11.claim: Mujahid says ifk means a lie: they worship idols and fabricate falsehood.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r11.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الإفك الكذب، والمعنى تعبدون الأوثان وتخلقون الكذب

QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r12.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r12.claim: Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman has a reading of the verb recorded as wa-takhluqūn.

QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r13.claim: Two further forms are reported: one intensive form of khalaqa, and one from takhallaqa meaning to lie or invent.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r13.anchor: وقرىء: { تخلقون } بمعنى التكثير من خلق و { تخلقون } من تخلق

QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r14.claim: Afkan has two analyses: a verbal noun like kadhib or laʿib, with ifk as its lightened form; or an adjective meaning a false creation.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r14.anchor: وقرىء: { أفكا } وفيه وجهان: أن يكون مصدرا نحو كذب ولعب

QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r15.claim: Awthānan is the object of taʿbudūna, and mā is an inna-blocking particle.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r15.anchor: و { أوثانا } نصب ب { تعبدون } و { ما } كافة

QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r16.claim: Outside the Qur’anic reading, awthān may be nominative if mā is taken as inna’s noun, taʿbudūn as its relative clause, and awthān as its predicate.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r16.anchor: ويجوز في غير القرآن رفع أوثان على أن تجعل { ما } اسما لأن

QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r17.claim: The phrase wa-takhluqūna ifkan is accusative through the verb alone.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r17.anchor: فأما { وتخلقون إفكا } فهو منصوب بالفعل لا غير

QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r18.claim: The idols cannot provide sustenance; direct hopes and requests for provision to God alone.
QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r18.anchor: أي اصرفوا رغبتكم في أرزاقكم إلى الله فإياه فاسألوه وحده
